title: The Cruel Reality of Long Covid-19

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: Even as rapidly expanding vaccinations offer a pathway out of the pandemic, there is a small group of people for whom the virus's lingering effects never seem to end.
sentences.zh: 尽管疫苗接种的迅速普及为走出疫情提供了途径，但仍有一小部分人似乎永远无法摆脱病毒带来的挥之不去的影响。

sentences.en: My colleague, Pam Bellick, on a rare and cruel case of long COVID.
sentences.zh: 我的同事帕姆·贝利克将讲述一个罕见且残酷的长新冠病例。

sentences.en: It's Monday, March 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月22日，星期一。

sentences.en: Well, take your time, and wherever you want to start is fine with me.
sentences.zh: 好的，慢慢来，你想从哪里开始都可以。

sentences.en: Pam, tell me about Ivan.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，跟我说说伊万的事吧。

sentences.en: Ivan Agerton is 50 years old.
sentences.zh: 伊万·阿格顿今年50岁。

sentences.en: He lives on Bainbridge Island outside of Seattle with his wife Emily and their three children.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子艾米丽以及三个孩子住在西雅图郊外的班布里奇岛上。

sentences.en: He's a former Marine, and he has an incredibly cool job.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名海军陆战队员，而且拥有一份非常酷的工作。

sentences.en: He is a photographer, and he does a lot of adventure photography and a lot of expeditions.
sentences.zh: 他是一名摄影师，经常从事探险摄影和各种考察活动。

sentences.en: And his most recent expedition was last fall.
sentences.zh: 他最近的一次考察是在去年秋天。

sentences.en: He spent two months in the Red Sea in a submarine.
sentences.zh: 他在红海的一艘潜水艇里待了两个月。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Doing photography and cinematography of all sorts of natural wonders and things that they were discovering down there.
sentences.zh: 拍摄各种自然奇观以及他们在海底发现的东西。

sentences.en: So he spent two months in a submarine in the middle of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以他在疫情期间在潜水艇里待了两个月。

sentences.en: Pretty intense, yeah.
sentences.zh: 相当紧张，是吧。

sentences.en: The team took a lot of very strict COVID precautions, lots of testing.
sentences.zh: 团队采取了非常严格的防疫措施，进行了大量的检测。

sentences.en: He tests negative as the expedition ends.
sentences.zh: 考察结束时，他的检测结果呈阴性。

sentences.en: And he has to take two or three flights from Saudi Arabia to get back to Seattle.
sentences.zh: 然后他必须从沙特阿拉伯转乘两三次航班才能回到西雅图。

sentences.en: And he gets home a little bit before Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 他在感恩节前不久回到了家。

sentences.en: And he goes and gets COVID tested.
sentences.zh: 他去做了新冠检测。

sentences.en: And it turns out that he is positive.
sentences.zh: 结果显示呈阳性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He doesn't have a very serious case.
sentences.zh: 他的病情并不严重。

sentences.en: Mild respiratory symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 只有轻微的呼吸道症状。

sentences.en: He loses his sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 他失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: So this is all sounding pretty routine and pretty run-of-the-mill as COVID infections go.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来这就像是常规的新冠感染，没什么特别的。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And in fact, it sounds like he's pretty lucky.
sentences.zh: 事实上，听起来他还是挺幸运的。

sentences.en: So then, a few days later, he gets kind of an ordinary spam phone call on his cell phone.
sentences.zh: 然而几天后，他的手机接到了一通普通的垃圾电话。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Who is this?
sentences.zh: 这是谁？

sentences.en: For some reason, this triggered sort of a cascade of paranoia and delusions.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，这引发了一连串的偏执和妄想。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Surveilling me.
sentences.zh: 在监视我。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, he is convinced that people are spying on him.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他确信有人在监视他。

sentences.en: And then I started thinking that people were listening to my phone.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始觉得有人在监听我的电话。

sentences.en: And so I downloaded it.
sentences.zh: 所以我下载了它。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He's really starting to kind of unravel.
sentences.zh: 他真的开始有点崩溃了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so I finally...
sentences.zh: 所以我终于……

sentences.en: And so after keeping this to himself for about 48 hours, he decides that he really needs to tell his wife what's going on.
sentences.zh: 在独自承受了大约48小时后，他决定必须告诉妻子发生了什么。

sentences.en: I know this is going to sound crazy, but, you know, I believe people are following me.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很疯狂，但我相信有人在跟踪我。

sentences.en: And the, you know, just his eyes terrifying, I felt like...
sentences.zh: 你知道，他的眼神太可怕了，我觉得……

sentences.en: Emily is just stunned.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽惊呆了。

sentences.en: She's shocked.
sentences.zh: 她感到震惊。

sentences.en: This is a man she's been married to for 18 years.
sentences.zh: 这是她结婚18年的丈夫。

sentences.en: He is unflappable, very calm in a crisis.
sentences.zh: 他平时处变不惊，在危机中非常冷静。

sentences.en: And she's just really trying to figure out what to make of this all.
sentences.zh: 她真的在努力弄清楚这一切到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: So Emily now is trying to figure out how to help Ivan.
sentences.zh: 所以艾米丽现在正试图想办法帮助伊万。

sentences.en: So for a day or two, she's trying to help him on her own.
sentences.zh: 起初一两天，她试图独自帮助他。

sentences.en: And she's doing things like taking him to Costco because she thought, well, if we go to
sentences.zh: 她做了一些事情，比如带他去好市多，因为她想，如果我们去

sentences.en: Costco, you know, it'll just be kind of like a normal Sunday afternoon and kind of get him out of this trauma that he's experiencing.
sentences.zh: 好市多，你知道，那就像一个普通的周日下午，或许能让他从这种创伤中走出来。

sentences.en: But that completely backfires because he becomes convinced that the shoppers are kind of plainclothes agents that are watching him.
sentences.zh: 但这完全适得其反，因为他开始确信购物者是监视他的便衣特工。

sentences.en: So finally, she, in desperation, you know, she calls a friend of hers who's a nurse who has mental health experience.
sentences.zh: 最后，她绝望地给一位有心理健康护理经验的朋友打了电话。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, I totally, I totally understand.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，我完全理解。

sentences.en: So she drives Ivan to their, their local hospital emergency room and the doctors do a brain scan to rule out a brain tumor and they can't really quite diagnose it themselves.
sentences.zh: 于是她开车把伊万送到当地医院的急诊室，医生做了脑部扫描以排除脑肿瘤，但他们自己也无法确诊。

sentences.en: They're assuming that it may have something to do with the fact that he hasn't been sleeping well.
sentences.zh: 他们推测这可能与他睡眠不好有关。

sentences.en: So they send him home with sleeping pills.
sentences.zh: 于是他们给他开了安眠药让他回家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So scary.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Things keep getting worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 情况变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: So Emily starts realizing, you know, they really need some serious psychiatric help for him.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽开始意识到，他真的需要专业的精神科帮助。

sentences.en: And finally, her nurse friend finds a space for Ivan at a hospital in Seattle and they get in the car and they start heading there.
sentences.zh: 最后，她的护士朋友在西雅图的一家医院为伊万找到了床位，他们上了车，开始往那边赶。

sentences.en: Emily checked me into ER.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽帮我办理了急诊入院。

sentences.en: You know, of course, because of COVID protocols, Emily isn't allowed to stay with him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当然，由于防疫规定，艾米丽不能陪他待在一起。

sentences.en: So she has to leave.
sentences.zh: 所以她不得不离开。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: One of the first things that they do is they test him for COVID.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第一件事就是给他做新冠检测。

sentences.en: But they finally came back.
sentences.zh: 但他们终于回来了。

sentences.en: Well, he tested positive for COVID.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的新冠检测呈阳性。

sentences.en: And it just turns out that he is still COVID positive.
sentences.zh: 结果证明他仍然是新冠阳性。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: How long had it been since his first COVID positive test?
sentences.zh: 距离他第一次新冠阳性检测过去多久了？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's been probably about three and a half weeks at this point.
sentences.zh: 是的，到目前为止大概已经有三周半了。

sentences.en: Is that unusual?
sentences.zh: 这不寻常吗？

sentences.en: It feels a little unusual that he would still be positive.
sentences.zh: 他仍然呈阳性确实感觉有点不寻常。

sentences.en: It's not that unusual.
sentences.zh: 这并不算太罕见。

sentences.en: What it means most likely is that not that he's still contagious, but he probably has, you know, some bit of virus hanging around still in his body.
sentences.zh: 这意味着最有可能的情况不是他仍具传染性，而是他的体内可能还有一些残留的病毒。

sentences.en: And there are a number of patients who have that.
sentences.zh: 有很多患者都有这种情况。

sentences.en: So this is where the medical team starts to think, well, maybe these symptoms are COVID related.
sentences.zh: 所以医疗团队开始认为，这些症状可能与新冠有关。

sentences.en: They move him into a psych ward.
sentences.zh: 他们把他转到了精神科病房。

sentences.en: And he's there with some very, you know, severely psychiatrically ill patients.
sentences.zh: 他在那里和一些患有严重精神疾病的病人待在一起。

sentences.en: And they put him in a room.
sentences.zh: 他们把他安排在一个房间里。

sentences.en: And he spends a lot of time looking out the window at a parking structure that's outside the window.
sentences.zh: 他花了很多时间盯着窗外的一个停车楼看。

sentences.en: And he is convinced that people in a car there are there to get him.
sentences.zh: 他确信车里的人是来抓他的。

sentences.en: And he's also crying a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且他哭得很厉害。

sentences.en: He's weeping.
sentences.zh: 他在流泪。

sentences.en: He knows something is happening to him that's not real, but it feels real.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己身上发生的事情是不真实的，但感觉却很真实。

sentences.en: What's interesting is you seem to be describing a highly self-aware version of paranoia.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，你描述的似乎是一种高度自我意识的偏执。

sentences.en: Somebody who knows that what's happening to him should not be happening, but it's still happening.
sentences.zh: 一个人知道发生在他身上的事情不应该发生，但它确实在发生。

sentences.en: And it's horrifying.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And that is really very unusual for people who have psychosis, which is really what Ivan ends up being diagnosed with.
sentences.zh: 这对于患有精神病的人来说确实非常罕见，而这正是伊万最终被诊断出的病症。

sentences.en: You know, most people who are patients with psychosis either have some kind of chronic situation like schizophrenia
sentences.zh: 你知道，大多数精神病患者要么患有某种慢性疾病，比如精神分裂症，

sentences.en: or sometimes they're, you know, elderly people who have it as a part of their dementia.
sentences.zh: 要么有时是老年人，这是他们痴呆症的一部分。

sentences.en: And most of the time, patients are in that kind of psychotic realm and aren't realizing that there's another reality out there.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，患者处于那种精神错乱的状态，并没有意识到还有另一个现实存在。

sentences.en: But Ivan, it was almost like double torture for him because not only is he having these hallucinations and delusions,
sentences.zh: 但对伊万来说，这几乎是双重折磨，因为他不仅出现了这些幻觉和妄想，

sentences.en: but half of him is also saying, I'm having these horrible hallucinations and delusions.
sentences.zh: 而且他内心的一半也在说，我正在经历这些可怕的幻觉和妄想。

sentences.en: And why is this happening?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: So Ivan is in the hospital for eight days.
sentences.zh: 伊万在医院住了八天。

sentences.en: He misses Christmas with his wife and three kids.
sentences.zh: 他错过了和妻子及三个孩子的圣诞节。

sentences.en: And he's treated with an antipsychotic that gradually starts to kind of kick in.
sentences.zh: 他接受了抗精神病药物治疗，药物开始逐渐起效。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that he finds helpful is that he sort of buries himself in books to kind of take him out of what was happening.
sentences.zh: 他发现另一件有帮助的事情是，他沉浸在书本中，试图让自己从正在发生的事情中抽离出来。

sentences.en: All of that sort of starts to help him improve.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都开始帮助他好转。

sentences.en: Paranoia starts to lift.
sentences.zh: 偏执感开始消退。

sentences.en: And he is better enough that shortly before New Year's, he's able to return home.
sentences.zh: 他的情况好转了，在新年之前，他得以回家。

sentences.en: And I had my first conversation with him five days later.
sentences.zh: 五天后我与他进行了第一次谈话。

sentences.en: And it's clear at that point that Ivan and his medical team believe that whatever has been happening with him is connected to COVID.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上很清楚，伊万和他的医疗团队都认为他身上发生的一切都与新冠有关。

sentences.en: And thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你。

sentences.en: And yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thanks, Pam.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，帕姆。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 解锁《纽约时报》应用程序。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息，去探索《纽约时报》会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅用户每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《纽约时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Pam, you have been writing about the long-term effects of COVID-19 for many, many months now.
sentences.zh: 那么，帕姆，你已经撰写关于新冠肺炎的长期影响好几个月了。

sentences.en: How common is the kind of story that Ivan has described to you?
sentences.zh: 伊万向你描述的那种故事有多普遍？

sentences.en: Well, Ivan's story is pretty uncommon, but it is not unique.
sentences.zh: 嗯，伊万的故事相当罕见，但并非独一无二。

sentences.en: There have been probably at this point dozens of cases of COVID-linked psychosis reported around the world and in this country.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，全世界和我国已经报告了数十例与新冠相关的精神病病例。

sentences.en: And if you broaden that out to COVID-related brain effects and neurological effects, we are talking about a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 如果你将其扩展到与新冠相关的大脑影响和神经系统影响，那涉及的人数就非常多了。

sentences.en: The psychosis cases are really sort of an extreme version of a spectrum of different brain-related and neurological-related symptoms that many,
sentences.zh: 精神病病例实际上是许多新冠幸存者正在经历的一系列大脑和神经系统相关症状中，

sentences.en: many COVID survivors are experiencing.
sentences.zh: 一种极端表现。

sentences.en: And what are those brain-related symptoms?
sentences.zh: 那么那些与大脑相关的症状是什么？

sentences.en: Describe those.
sentences.zh: 描述一下那些症状。

sentences.en: So there have been a lot of reports of something that people are calling brain fog,
sentences.zh: 有很多关于人们称之为“脑雾”的报道，

sentences.en: which is sort of a collection of symptoms that involve things like forgetting what you went into the room for, you know, not being able to organize things,
sentences.zh: 这是一系列症状的集合，包括忘记自己走进房间是为了什么，你知道，无法组织事情，

sentences.en: not being able to do very, very simple tasks.
sentences.zh: 无法完成非常、非常简单的任务。

sentences.en: I have written about a man who had gone to Paris just before getting COVID and this whirlwind trip with his partner and now cannot remember a single thing about his trip to Paris.
sentences.zh: 我写过一个男人的故事，他在感染新冠前刚和伴侣去巴黎进行了一次旋风般的旅行，现在却对巴黎之行一点记忆都没有了。

sentences.en: He looks at pictures of him and his partner in front of the Mona Lisa and they're smiling and they're in front of the Eiffel Tower and he says, gosh,
sentences.zh: 他看着他和伴侣在蒙娜丽莎前的照片，他们微笑着，站在埃菲尔铁塔前，他说，天哪，

sentences.en: it looks like we were really having a good time, but I can't remember anything about it.
sentences.zh: 看起来我们当时玩得很开心，但我对那次旅行一点记忆都没有。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I've written about, you know, nurses who sort of forget what patients have told them the minute they leave the exam room,
sentences.zh: 我写过关于护士的事，你知道，她们在病人离开检查室的那一刻，就忘了病人刚才说了什么，

sentences.en: an operating room nurse who can't remember what a scalpel is called.
sentences.zh: 还有一位手术室护士，她记不起手术刀叫什么名字了。

sentences.en: So she says, you know, give me that thing that we cut with, that's brain fog.
sentences.zh: 所以她说，你知道，给我那个我们用来切割的东西，这就是脑雾。

sentences.en: And that is really just one of the brain-related neurological issues that people are experiencing.
sentences.zh: 这确实只是人们正在经历的与大脑相关的神经系统问题之一。

sentences.en: I mean, you've got people who are having trouble smelling and tasting or having phantom smells.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人出现了嗅觉和味觉障碍，或者出现了幻嗅。

sentences.en: There's a lot of people with muscle pain or muscle weakness or headaches and that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 很多人有肌肉疼痛、肌肉无力或头痛之类的症状。

sentences.en: And studies are starting to come out now that are finding 20%, 30%, maybe more of COVID survivors are experiencing one or more of these kinds of neurological issues.
sentences.zh: 现在的研究开始表明，20%、30%甚至更多的COVID幸存者正在经历一种或多种这类神经系统问题。

sentences.en: So it's going to be a problem for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以这在很长一段时间内都会是个问题。

sentences.en: And what exactly do scientists believe is happening here?
sentences.zh: 那么科学家们究竟认为这里发生了什么呢？

sentences.en: What is the virus doing to people to trigger these brain-related symptoms of the virus?
sentences.zh: 病毒对人体做了什么，从而引发了这些与大脑相关的病毒症状？

sentences.en: So there are a few theories that I would say nobody knows exactly yet, but basically what scientists think is happening is not that the virus is getting into people's brains.
sentences.zh: 有一些理论，我想说目前还没有人确切知道，但科学家们认为，基本上发生的并不是病毒进入了人们的大脑。

sentences.en: Instead, what it seems to be doing is that when you get infected with COVID, your body responds to the virus.
sentences.zh: 相反，看起来是当你感染了COVID时，你的身体会对病毒做出反应。

sentences.en: It tries to fight the virus, right?
sentences.zh: 它试图对抗病毒，对吧？

sentences.en: So you get an immune system response.
sentences.zh: 所以你会产生免疫系统反应。

sentences.en: And that immune system response generates inflammation.
sentences.zh: 而这种免疫系统反应会产生炎症。

sentences.en: And what they think is happening is that the body's inflammatory response is not just inflaming the body, but it can inflame what's going on in the brain as well.
sentences.zh: 他们认为发生的情况是，身体的炎症反应不仅会引起身体炎症，还会引起大脑内部的炎症。

sentences.en: And depending on where in the brain that inflammation is happening, it can affect a particular function or set of functions that the brain is used to doing.
sentences.zh: 根据炎症在大脑中发生的位置，它会影响大脑习惯执行的特定功能或功能集。

sentences.en: So maybe it's your memory, maybe it's ability to do kind of multitasking.
sentences.zh: 所以可能是你的记忆力，也可能是多任务处理的能力。

sentences.en: And in very extreme cases like Ivan's, it could have something to do with a psychiatric illness.
sentences.zh: 而在像伊万这样非常极端的案例中，它可能与精神疾病有关。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so in that sense, people like Ivan become victims of their body's own natural defenses.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，像伊万这样的人成了他们身体自身自然防御机制的受害者。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's the best theory that doctors have come up with.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是医生们提出的最好的理论。

sentences.en: And that theory is buttressed by not only what they're seeing with COVID, but for decades, there have been cases like this with other viruses.
sentences.zh: 而且这个理论不仅得到了他们在COVID中观察到的现象的支持，几十年来，其他病毒也出现过类似的病例。

sentences.en: It's from the 1918 flu pandemic to the SARS pandemic to MERS to meningitis.
sentences.zh: 从1918年流感大流行到SARS大流行，再到MERS和脑膜炎。

sentences.en: There are these cases that they call sort of post-viral psychosis.
sentences.zh: 这些病例被称为病毒后精神病。

sentences.en: And they're different than typical psychosis.
sentences.zh: 它们与典型的精神病不同。

sentences.en: And they affect often people like Ivan who don't seem to have any other mental health history.
sentences.zh: 它们经常影响像伊万这样似乎没有任何其他心理健康病史的人。

sentences.en: Pam, I recognize that this is all very new.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，我知道这一切都很新。

sentences.en: So with that caveat, what is the understanding of how long a COVID-related brain symptom like what Ivan has been dealing with is expected to last?
sentences.zh: 那么在有此提醒的前提下，对于像伊万正在处理的这种COVID相关脑部症状，预计会持续多久？

sentences.en: Do we know?
sentences.zh: 我们知道吗？

sentences.en: This is really uncharted territory.
sentences.zh: 这真的是未知的领域。

sentences.en: No, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不知道。

sentences.en: You know, we've had a smattering of cases so far.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到目前为止我们只遇到过零星的病例。

sentences.en: Some of them have needed several weeks of treatment and they've tried several different kinds of medications.
sentences.zh: 其中一些需要几周的治疗，他们尝试了几种不同的药物。

sentences.en: And then some people have gotten better.
sentences.zh: 然后有些人好转了。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 还好。

sentences.en: How are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你最近怎么样？

sentences.en: There have been cases where people have had relapses.
sentences.zh: 也有过人们复发的病例。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that, unfortunately, is what happened to Ivan.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这就是伊万发生的情况。

sentences.en: By mid-January, he had told me that he was actually feeling 100% better, no paranoia.
sentences.zh: 到一月中旬，他告诉我他感觉已经100%好转了，没有偏执妄想。

sentences.en: And his psychiatrist said he was doing really well.
sentences.zh: 他的精神科医生也说他做得很好。

sentences.en: But in the second week of February, Ivan reached out to me.
sentences.zh: 但在二月的第二周，伊万联系了我。

sentences.en: It was a headline, you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是因为一个新闻标题吗？

sentences.en: He had seen a headline about a police raid and just triggered everything.
sentences.zh: 他看到了一个关于警方突袭的新闻标题，这直接触发了一切。

sentences.en: And he said, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 他说，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: The paranoia came screaming back.
sentences.zh: 偏执妄想又尖叫着回来了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And the day after I talked to him, he was admitted to the psych ward and the hospital again.
sentences.zh: 在我和他谈话后的第二天，他又被送进了精神病院。

sentences.en: That must have been really crushing to he and his wife.
sentences.zh: 这对他的妻子和他来说一定非常令人崩溃。

sentences.en: It was devastating.
sentences.zh: 那是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: This relapse and this whole experience feels like such a powerful reminder that the coronavirus has only been with us for a year.
sentences.zh: 这次复发和整个经历感觉像是一个强有力的提醒，冠状病毒陪伴我们才一年。

sentences.en: And there just seems to be so much that we really don't know about.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎还有太多我们真的不知道的事情。

sentences.en: And as a result,
sentences.zh: 结果就是，

sentences.en: it feels like Ivan and anybody who's just kind of an outlier becomes this really horrible real-life case study that the rest of us are kind of poking and prodding and studying to try to understand.
sentences.zh: 感觉伊万和任何像他这样的个例，都成了我们其他人为了试图理解而不断探究和研究的非常可怕的现实案例。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, there's just so much that we don't know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，还有太多我们不知道的事情。

sentences.en: We don't know who gets these long-term symptoms and why.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道谁会患上这些长期症状，也不知道为什么。

sentences.en: You know, it's not just people with pre-existing conditions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不仅仅是针对有既往病史的人。

sentences.en: It's not just people who are hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是针对住院的人。

sentences.en: It's not just older people.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是针对老年人。

sentences.en: We don't know how long these things laSt.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这些症状会持续多久。

sentences.en: We don't know what recovery looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道康复是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And very importantly, we don't know what treatment works for many of these things.
sentences.zh: 而且非常重要的一点是，我们不知道什么治疗方法对其中许多问题有效。

sentences.en: And for the brain-related issues, it's even more difficult because for people who are having, say, heart problems or lung issues after COVID, those are serious and troublesome.
sentences.zh: 对于大脑相关的问题，情况甚至更困难，因为对于那些在COVID之后出现心脏问题或肺部问题的人来说，这些问题虽然严重且令人困扰，

sentences.en: But there are heart medications and there are lung medications and there are a lot of things that we know that can help.
sentences.zh: 但有心脏药物，有肺部药物，我们知道有很多东西可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: But there's no pill that you can take to clear your brain fog, you know.
sentences.zh: 但没有一种药丸可以让你消除脑雾，你知道的。

sentences.en: And so it's really very complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很复杂。

sentences.en: There's been one kind of glimmer of potential hope in this area, which is that there are some people with long COVID who are reporting that after they get the COVID vaccine,
sentences.zh: 在这个领域出现了一丝潜在的希望，那就是有一些患有长期COVID的人报告说，在接种COVID疫苗后，

sentences.en: their symptoms are improving and in some cases vanishing.
sentences.zh: 他们的症状正在改善，在某些情况下甚至消失了。

sentences.en: And I've had several people tell me these wonderful stories of having like this terrible brain fog for months and months and they get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 我有几个人告诉我这些美妙的故事，说他们几个月来一直有这种可怕的脑雾，然后他们接种了疫苗。

sentences.en: And then, you know, a few days later, it's like, oh, what a beautiful morning.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，几天后，就像是，哦，多么美好的早晨。

sentences.en: You know, one woman told me that it was like she was directing Sweeney Todd for months.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一位女士告诉我，那感觉就像她执导了几个月的《理发师陶德》。

sentences.en: And now all of a sudden she's directing Oklahoma.
sentences.zh: 而现在突然间她开始执导《俄克拉荷马》。

sentences.en: So that's a very, very theatrical joke.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一个非常、非常戏剧性的笑话。

sentences.en: But she's gone from deep darkness to something brighter.
sentences.zh: 但她已经从深沉的黑暗走向了更明亮的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And it's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: I think maybe we will find that some subset of people with long COVID are helped.
sentences.zh: 我想也许我们会发现，一部分患有长期COVID的人会得到帮助。

sentences.en: So has Ivan gotten his vaccine?
sentences.zh: 那么伊万接种疫苗了吗？

sentences.en: Is there any hope that that might do something for him?
sentences.zh: 有什么希望这对他会有所帮助吗？

sentences.en: No, not yet.
sentences.zh: 不，还没有。

sentences.en: But I'm really happy to report that he's home again.
sentences.zh: 但我很高兴地报告，他又回家了。

sentences.en: He's feeling much better.
sentences.zh: 他感觉好多了。

sentences.en: He's not 100 percent, but he's getting there.
sentences.zh: 他还没有完全恢复，但他正在好转。

sentences.en: I still don't have my sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 我仍然没有嗅觉。

sentences.en: So something is still damaged in my brain.
sentences.zh: 所以我的大脑里还有东西受损了。

sentences.en: And so once I recover my sense of smell, my guess is that that's when this will go away.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我恢复了嗅觉，我猜这就是它消失的时候。

sentences.en: And that my brain will be healthy and back to normal.
sentences.zh: 我的大脑就会健康并恢复正常。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不知道。

sentences.en: That's just a layman's.
sentences.zh: 这只是外行人的看法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, I hope that's what I'm kind of looking forward to.
sentences.zh: 不，我希望这就是我所期待的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And he's just, you know, really hopeful that he'll be back to the old Ivan again.
sentences.zh: 他只是，你知道，真的希望他能变回以前的伊万。

sentences.en: I'm tired of picking up the dog shit, too.
sentences.zh: 我也厌倦了去捡狗屎。

sentences.en: So I can't smell it.
sentences.zh: 因为我闻不到它。

sentences.en: I have to pick it up now.
sentences.zh: 我现在不得不去捡它。

sentences.en: So, but, you know, there's something to look forward to, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以，但是，你知道，我想还是有值得期待的事情的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But it's still there still is that underlying fear that, fuck, I mean, how long is this going to take, you know?
sentences.zh: 但仍然存在那种潜在的恐惧，该死，我的意思是，这需要多长时间，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他内容。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由奥斯汀·米切尔制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Dave Shaw and Lisa Chow and engineered by Corey Shreppel.
sentences.zh: 由戴夫·肖和丽莎·周编辑，科里·施雷佩尔担任工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
